preamble: Fronting of the velar stop [k] to the alveolar stop [t] is best known as 'velar fronting' in child speech, a common developmental process in English-speaking children (car > [tɑː]). As a historical change it is found in Hakka, where Middle Chinese velar codas -k became dental -t after front vowels.

examples.note: Developmental velar fronting, one of the phonological error patterns documented in normative studies of British English-speaking children.
Middle Chinese -k after front vowels became dental -t; Cantonese keeps the velar (sik6).

sources: Dodd, B., Holm, A., Hua, Z., & Crosbie, S. (2003). Phonological development: a normative study of British English-speaking children. Clinical Linguistics & Phonetics, 17(8), 617–643. https://doi.org/10.1080/0269920031000111348
